## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [15. November 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.63
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.63
- Datum: 15.11.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
on the way from Buenos Aires to Rio 15. Nov. Dear Hannah and Manfred, now in the
aeroplane we have the first moment since three weeks. The strain was large, yesterday
at 10 30 I read still broadcast, we came home at midnight where a cinema agent was waiting for me.
In the morning at 5 we had to get up and found at six the same agent waiting, now we are
on the way, after being ~~photographed~~ {been} for the thousands and last time. I had altogether ten
lectures instead of four in these three weeks and we have doubled the fees of the last ones
except the one in English and one in German I gave for charity purposes. And then the table
needs, the interviews, the cinephotos, the travels - I have at least made the tour round the
world - yesterday still Uruguay, going and returning by plane: poor Lotte was frightfully
tired even without having accompanied me in the most strenuous voyages in the province.
But now it is over. I have earned enough in these three hard weeks that we can now pass
the next three month in our modest way and do some work. I am longing to have some
quiet time without publicity. And whenever I want to take up again the lecturing
I can do it, I have invitations to Paraguay, Cuba, Columbia, Chile and I do not know
how many countries and of course here and in Uruguay again. But we will stay for
two months at least in Brasil and see how we can stand the climate in summer, pro-
bably we shall retire in the mountains (the only difficulty is to find a hotel there with
a little comfort and quietness, as all Rio moves at the same time to these places)
As to Freivental I wrote you, that I had a private audience at the Minister of
Foreign Affairs who at my request granted me three visas, two for my former pub-
lishers in Holland and one for Freivental; as I hear the cables have gone already to
the respective consulates. I am nevertheless not quite sure, that all will go smoothly
as every time we ourselves had to do with visas there were always delays and
something forgotten; if it should not be delivered to him, please cable that I may
remind here. I remember how complicated it was to transform our visitors visa
to Brasil in a permanent one and you may imagine that all was well prepared for
us, but always there is something forgotten or a detail wanting in these bureaucratic
times; now all is in perfect order for us and we want no more special permissions
to go in and out of Brasil and can ever stay as long as we want
All what you write about our house in Bath is very reconforting; please do not forget
that you can make me personally a great pleasure and that is in disposing of all
my belongings for you and your family as if it were yours. It is a great satis-
faction for me to know that it is useful to somebody - and especially to people
like you - while it is totally useless to me. Please remember this always. And
Manfred shall have from time to time a rest. Who knows what is expecting still us all
and only one thing is really wise for the future - to keep fit, to have his body and
his brains in good order. As to Eidamaca I am afraid that the death of our

pages.transcription:
from Hernandez Cata will prove fatal to his Cuban visa as it was
Cata who gave the garanties for him and now the only man who could urge if there
was some hindrance or delay, is gone. I am so sorry for Eisemann that it did
not work immediately as Cata and I had hoped, but perhaps there will be another
opportunity. A bookseller of Buenos Aires wired him for books and they are already
in touch - here is a lot of wealth but the people in Argentine have not yet learned
to spend it in cultural things, they begin now smoothly. The country is not very inspi-
ring and both Lotte and I prefer Brasil which is picturesk and has a great charm
in the landscape and in the people. I hope you will know it a day. And now I leave
the sheet to Lotte, who is again allright and will write you all I have forgotten
to tell you about Argentine and Uruguay (where the abundance of food and the
quietness of life has for us Europeans somewhat exciting) Yours Stefan
Dear Hanna and Manfred, We received yesterday both Hanna's letter with the copy of
Eva's first letter and yours, Manfred which was very interesting. I am happy and
grateful to know her safe and well, and if she does not like my family-
in-law, she exaggerates perhaps but is not altogether wrong. I was glad
to know that you were both all-right so far, but I would feel better
if you were both away from London. When do you give up Woodstock Road?
- We are glad to return to Rio and we are determined to live quietly there
and to work. I am only sorry that I did not bring a new Royal Portable Typewriter
with me, mine is beginning to wear out, although still incomparably better than
your brother's. Has Heiner got all the papers for the affidavit now? You did not
mention it and I only had information from Newyork that he had send a cable
confirming the receipt of the affidavit and that the forms had been sent by registered
airmail from Buenos Aires. Stefan's first wife and most of his colleagues have been able
to get out of France and are now in Newyork. In South Am. there are few newcomers
as visas to all the countries are almost impossible to get. About our journey to
Argentine I shall write more later on when my impressions have settled down. For the
moment I only remember the meat portions were enormous, the weather
continually changing from hot to cold, the telephone continually ringing,
Stefan giving one lecture after the other and little speeches in between,
myself continually dead-tired and our time taken by all sorts of things
from early morning to late at night. From Uruguay my principal impressions
were the first flight by hydro-avion and the fact that we did not speak
anything but Spanish and that fortunately ladies were excluded from the
banquet after the lecture. Best wishes and kisses and kindest regards
to the Rosemount - and Woodstock inhabitants Lotte
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf gelbem Papier. Fortsetzung des Briefes.
Rückseite der dritten Seite mit aufgelegter Farb- und Grauskala zur Archivierung.
